title: Traffic Failsafe Slate — prototype for staged recovery and rollback affordances
creator: Marisol Ortega
description: Design a lightweight, discoverable UI pattern (the 'Failsafe Slate') for the Redwood Console that makes it easy to define staged rollouts (canary + A/B), author traffic-splits, and declare automated failsafe/rollback rules. The artifact should include a compact builder flow, a clear visualization of live traffic shards, and an escalation panel for emergency rollbacks that reduces time-to-recover. Goal: decrease operator cognitive load during incidents and make safe defaults obvious for PM/Engineers onboarding to Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype for the Failsafe Slate covering: define variant weights, set metric-based safety gates, and configure emergency rollback triggers
Visualization shows live traffic distribution, recent metric deltas, and per-variant error hotspots
Emergency rollback flow can be completed in <= 3 clicks from slate, with a confirmation modal that surfaces expected impact and dependent routes
Design annotated with accessibility contrast checks and keyboard-first interactions
Design decisions and trade-offs documented and reviewed by Eng and PM
Prototype validated by at least 3 engineering and 3 product stakeholders in a walkthrough session
comments: 2026-02-12 Marisol Ortega: Kickoff — sketched three candidate layouts: split list, timeline taper, and a compact canvas. Decided to prototype compact slate + expandable detail panel to reduce layout churn on Console home pages.

2026-02-18 Evan Patel: Implemented first-click flows in Figma. Engineering concern: telemetry payload to render per-variant error hotspots will need sampling. Filed PR for metrics aggregation (see pull_requests).

2026-02-23 Priya Shah (PM): Questioned whether emergency rollback should always be global vs variant-specific. Decision: allow both, surface global rollback more prominently but keep variant rollback inline to reduce accidental full-service rollbacks.
2026-02-26 Design review: Accessibility flagged color ramp insufficient for red/amber states on low-contrast monitors — updated palette and added iconography + text labels for state redundancy.
2026-02-27 Eng review (J. Wu): Raised race condition around concurrent rollouts; proposed optimistic-lock UI state and explicit conflict modal. Added to tradeoffs and next steps.

2026-03-01 Research (Ben Holt): Quick moderated usability session (n=5) — users locate rollback in 2.4 clicks average, asked for clearer pre-rollback impact estimate. Added 'estimated affected qps' line to confirmation modal.
2026-03-02 Evan Patel: Prototype updated with live-data wiring stub; moving to In Review for cross-functional signoff. Scheduling follow-up with SRE for emergency runbook alignment.
decisions: Use a single-line 'Slate' card in the rollouts list that expands into a right-side panel for variant and safety rule editing.
Show live traffic distribution as stacked horizontal bars with per-variant error rate overlays rather than separate charts to preserve vertical real-estate.
Emergency rollback flow is two-step: (1) immediate isolate (route 0% traffic to variant) + (2) optional full revert. Both actions surface estimated token/requests impact before confirmation.
Fallback automation: when telemetry latency > 10s, hide live heatmaps and surface last-known snapshot with a yellow warning state.
Keyboard-first affordances: all major actions accessible via keyboard shortcuts; primary destructive action requires typed confirmation (variant name) to prevent accidental triggers.
tradeoffs: Compact slate conserves space on listing pages but increases density in the expanded panel; we mitigated with collapsible sub-sections.
Stacked bar + overlay reduces visual clutter but can obscure small-variant signals; mitigated by tooltips and focus-on-hover zoom.
Showing 'estimated affected qps' requires accurate request mapping which may lag in Private deployments; we display best-effort estimates with clear confidence badges.
